newsitem.title: RUSSIA: FOCUS-Russian stocks, bonds rise on ratings.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Russian stocks, bonds rise on ratings.

text.p: Russian stocks and bonds rose on Monday on better than expected credit ratings for the country's foreign currency debt and analysts said prices could go higher.
Shares were also boosted by the announcement of the preliminary price for an international issue for Gazprom, the world's biggest gas company and Russia's biggest company by market capitalisation.
"The ratings are very positive and change the benchmark against which Russia is going to be measured," said Loren Bough, American Depositary Reeceipts trader at Brunswick Brokerage.
Dealers said shares, which rose slightly in the morning, jumped by about one percent after the ratings were announced.

"It looks like New York is very enthused over this news," said Nick Mokhoff, head trader at Alliance-Menatep. "I anticipate there will be support out of the States and continued support tomorrow as well."
Prices for Ministry of Finance bonds, or MinFins, rose one percentage point after the ratings, which are seen as a pre-requisite for Russia's planned debut Eurobond issue.
"People are buying everything," an International Moscow Bank dealer said.
Standard & Poor's gave Russia a BB- long-term rating, Moody's Investors Services set a Ba2 ceiling for long-term foreign currency bonds and IBCA gave it a BB+ long-term foreign currency rating.
"It means that the world economic community confirmed its support and its understanding that Russia is moving in a good direction," Finance Minister Alexander Livshits told a news conference.
Russian dollar-denominated Vneshekonombank debt also rose sharply after the ratings, which were just below investment grade. Vnesh loans were at 78.625, up 4.25 points from Friday.
Charles Blitzer, chief economist, emerging markets, at Donaldson, Lufkin and Jenrette, said Russian debt paper still looked undervalued with spreads wider than countries with similar ratings.
"There is significant upside potential as the spreads on Russian paper move towards Latin American levels," he said.

Stocks firmed in early trade after lead managers Morgan Stanley and Dresdner Kleinwort Benson said the preliminary price for an issue of 23.7 million American Depositary Shares in Gazprom would be between $14 and $16 each.

One ADS represents 10 shares. Gazprom shares are highly illiquid but analysts say its vast reserves of gas, accounting for 23 percent of global supply, should ensure the issue is a success despite the premium over the underlying share price.
Gazprom closed at $0.345 on the Russian Trading System, after $0.330 at Friday's close.

"The combination of the ratings and a successful Gazprom deal at a reasonable price are big credibility enhancers for the Russian market in the next two to three months and help negate the effects of (President Boris) Yeltsin's health problems," said Bough.

Share prices, which rose sharply in the run-up to Yeltsin's re-election in July, have been depressed by the 65-year-old leader's health problems and speculation over power struggles in his absence. Yeltsin is awaiting heart surgery.

"We still have the whole Yeltsin situation that is keeping people a little bit shy at this point but the fact that the fixed income market reacted so well certainly will give a boost to the equity market and already has," said Mokhoff.
